## Root cause

`src/context.ts:414-434` — when reassigning `c.res`, the merge loop ran `_res.headers.delete('set-cookie')` before appending only `this.#res`'s cookies. That wiped the **new** response's own Set-Cookie headers. Because this runtime's `Headers.entries()` yields one entry per `set-cookie`, the old block also re-deleted/re-appended on each pass.

## Fix — `src/context.ts:414-434`

```ts
for (const [k, v] of this.#res.headers.entries()) {
  if (k === 'content-type' || k === 'set-cookie') {
    continue
  }
  _res.headers.set(k, v)
}
// Merge `set-cookie` headers, keeping the cookies of the previous `c.res` first
// and then appending the cookies of the newly assigned Response, so that
// neither side's cookies are lost or duplicated.
const newCookies = _res.headers.getSetCookie()
_res.headers.delete('set-cookie')
for (const cookie of [...this.#res.headers.getSetCookie(), ...newCookies]) {
  _res.headers.append('set-cookie', cookie)
}
```

- Cookies are captured from the new response **once**, before deletion, so nothing is lost.
- Old-then-new ordering matches the existing `#newResponse` merge path (`src/context.ts:614-625`).
- No duplication regardless of whether `entries()` yields combined or per-cookie `set-cookie` entries.
- All other header behavior (`content-type` skip, `set` for the rest) is unchanged.
